title: Capacity and Margin
scenario: A manufacturer sells Product X for $90 per unit; variable cost is $52 per unit and each unit requires 2 machine hours. Product Y sells for $120 per unit; variable cost is $72 and each unit requires 3 machine hours. Machine hours are the single binding constraint, with unmet demand for both products and no other differential effects.

questions.q: Which product has the higher contribution margin per unit?
questions.explanation: X contributes $38; Y contributes $48 per unit.

questions.q: Which product has the higher contribution margin per machine hour?

choices.C: Both have the same contribution per machine hour
choices.D: Prioritize solely by contribution per unit, regardless of machine time

questions.explanation: X: $38/2=$19 per hour; Y: $48/3=$16 per hour.

title: Project Evaluation
scenario: A company is evaluating a project requiring $200,000 initially. Expected annual after-tax cash inflows are $80,000 for three years. Required return is 10%. Ignore salvage value. For fractional simple payback, assume the annual cash inflows are received uniformly within each year.

questions.q: Ignoring discounting, what is simple payback?
Why is NPV preferred over simple payback for value-creation decisions?

choices.A: NPV excludes cash flows after the payback date
choices.B: NPV measures accounting income rather than cash flows
choices.D: NPV considers the time value of money and all modeled project cash flows

questions.explanation: NPV discounts all relevant project cash flows at an appropriate required return. Simple payback neither discounts cash flows nor measures benefits received after recovery of the initial investment.

title: Flexible Budget Review
scenario: A service company prepared a monthly static budget for 10,000 service hours. Budgeted variable operating costs are $18 per hour and budgeted fixed operating costs are $90,000. Actual activity was 12,000 hours and actual operating costs were $315,000.

questions.q: What is the flexible-budget operating cost for 12,000 hours?
Compared with the flexible budget, actual operating costs produced what variance?
questions.explanation: Actual $315,000 minus flexible budget $306,000 equals a $9,000 unfavorable variance.

title: Special Order Decision
scenario: A company has unused production capacity. A customer offers to buy 4,000 units for $42 each. Variable manufacturing cost is $27 per unit, and the special order would add $3 per unit of shipping cost. No fixed costs would change, and accepting the order would not reduce normal sales.

questions.q: What is the incremental contribution per special-order unit?
questions.explanation: Incremental revenue $42 less variable manufacturing $27 and shipping $3 equals $12 per unit.

questions.q: What is the total incremental operating income from accepting the order?
questions.explanation: $12 incremental contribution × 4,000 units = $48,000.

title: Flexible budget vs. static budget
scenario: A manufacturer budgeted 10,000 units but produced and sold 9,000. Static cost budget $500,000: $30 variable cost per unit plus $200,000 fixed. Actual total manufacturing cost was $460,000.

questions.q: What is the flexible cost budget at actual volume?
What is the flexible-budget cost variance?
questions.explanation: $470,000 flexible cost less $460,000 actual cost = $10,000 favorable.

title: Master Budget and Sales Forecast
scenario: A manufacturer plans to sell 12,000 units next quarter at $50 each. Beginning finished goods inventory is 1,500 units and management wants ending finished goods inventory of 2,000 units. Variable manufacturing cost is $28 per unit; quarterly fixed manufacturing costs are $90,000.

questions.q: What is budgeted production in units?
questions.explanation: Budgeted production = sales 12,000 + desired ending inventory 2,000 − beginning inventory 1,500 = 12,500 units.

questions.q: What is budgeted manufacturing cost for the quarter?
questions.explanation: Variable manufacturing cost is 12,500 units × $28 = $350,000. Add fixed manufacturing costs of $90,000 for $440,000 total.

title: Direct material and labor variances
scenario: Standards: direct material 3 lb per unit at $5/lb; direct labor 2 hours per unit at $20/hour. Actual output 4,000 units; purchased 13,000 lb at $4.80; used 12,500 lb; labor 8,200 hours at $20.50.

questions.q: What is the materials purchase-price variance?
questions.explanation: ($4.80 − $5) × 13,000 lb purchased = $2,600 favorable.

questions.q: What is the materials usage variance?
questions.explanation: (12,500 used − 4,000 × 3 allowed) × $5 = $2,500 unfavorable.

questions.q: What is the labor rate variance?
What is the labor efficiency variance?
questions.explanation: (8,200 − 8,000 allowed hours) × $20 = $4,000 unfavorable.

title: ROI vs. residual income
scenario: Division X has operating income $900,000 and average operating assets $5,000,000. Hurdle rate 12%. A new project costs $1,000,000 and earns annual operating income $150,000.

questions.q: What are the division's current ROI and residual income?
Which decision best aligns with corporate value creation?

choices.A: Reject because project ROI is below current divisional ROI
choices.B: Reject because residual income is negative
choices.C: Accept because project ROI exceeds 12% and adds $30,000 residual income
choices.D: Accept only if project ROI exceeds 18%

questions.explanation: Project ROI is 15% and project RI is $150,000 − 12% × $1,000,000 = $30,000. Accepting increases value.

title: Traditional costing vs. ABC
scenario: Total overhead $900,000 allocated traditionally over 50,000 direct labor hours: Product H uses 40,000, L uses 10,000. ABC pools: setups $300,000 (H 20, L 130); machining $400,000 (H 35,000 hours, L 5,000); engineering $200,000 (H 100 hours, L 900).

questions.q: How much traditional overhead is assigned to Product H?
How much ABC overhead is assigned to Product H?
questions.explanation: Setups $40,000 + machining $350,000 + engineering $20,000 = $410,000.

title: Joint costs and further processing
scenario: Joint cost $240,000 produces X (8,000 units at $25 split-off price) and Y (4,000 units at $30 split-off price, or $45 after further processing at $8/unit).

questions.q: Using sales value at split-off, how much joint cost is allocated to X?
What is the incremental profit from further processing Y?
questions.explanation: 4,000 × ($45 − $30 − $8) = $28,000. Joint costs are irrelevant to this decision.

title: US GAAP to IFRS conversion
scenario: A US manufacturer is converting to IFRS. Its inventory uses LIFO with a $2 million LIFO reserve; a $3 million inventory write-down has recovered $1 million; $5 million development costs meet IFRS capitalization criteria.

questions.q: Which inventory method is prohibited under IFRS?
questions.explanation: IFRS prohibits LIFO. The LIFO reserve indicates the adjustment between LIFO and a non-LIFO basis, subject to conversion specifics.

questions.q: What is the permitted IFRS treatment of a qualifying inventory write-down recovery?

choices.B: Reverse the recovered amount up to the original write-down
choices.C: Recognize the recovery only upon sale

questions.explanation: IAS 2 allows reversal when the reasons for a prior write-down no longer exist, limited to the original write-down.

title: ASC 606 allocation
scenario: Software contract price $1.2 million, including a distinct license delivered at signing and distinct implementation services over six months. Standalone prices: license $1,000,000; services $250,000. Cash received at signing.

questions.q: What transaction price is allocated to the license?
questions.explanation: $1.2 million × ($1 million/$1.25 million) = $960,000, assuming the distinct license transfers at signing.

questions.q: How much service revenue is recognized per month over six months?
questions.explanation: Allocated services price $240,000 / 6 months = $40,000 monthly.

title: Control deficiencies at a manufacturer
scenario: A 40-person manufacturer has one bookkeeper who signs checks under $5,000, posts to the ledger, and reconciles the bank. Warehouse staff count inventory without independent recount. Purchases below $5,000 receive no review.

questions.q: Which is the clearest segregation-of-duties deficiency?

choices.B: Bookkeeper signs checks, records transactions, and reconciles bank

questions.explanation: Combining cash authorization/custody, recordkeeping, and reconciliation undermines independent control.

questions.q: Which improvement best addresses cash disbursement risk?

choices.A: Have the bookkeeper also approve all vendors
choices.D: Have an independent person review reconciliations and approve disbursements

questions.explanation: Independent review and authorization compensate for limited staffing and separate incompatible duties.

title: Cash-receipts controls
scenario: A 200-employee company with a centralized accounting department wants stronger controls over incoming payments and receivables.

questions.q: Which is primarily a detective cash-receipts control?
questions.explanation: Independent reconciliation identifies errors or irregularities after processing; the other choices are preventive.

questions.q: Which duties should be separated?

choices.A: Cash custody and recordkeeping can always be combined
choices.C: Cash custody, accounts receivable posting, and bank reconciliation
choices.D: No separation is needed if an ERP is installed

questions.explanation: Separating custody, recording, and reconciliation reduces opportunity to conceal diversion of receipts.

title: ERP selection and implementation
scenario: A distributor is replacing disconnected accounting, inventory, and sales systems with an ERP. Implementation quotes range from $800,000 to $1.5 million over 18 months.

questions.q: Which implementation approach reduces disruption by rolling out one module or site first?
questions.explanation: Phased rollout allows stabilization and learning before broader deployment, though the right approach depends on dependencies.

questions.q: What should the controller own during ERP implementation?

choices.D: Financial requirements, embedded controls, data quality, and user acceptance testing

questions.explanation: Finance owns the control and data-quality outcomes, not necessarily the software code.

title: Building analytics maturity
scenario: A retail chain has monthly descriptive sales reports and wants to reduce stockouts and markdowns through more advanced analytics.

questions.q: Which analytics type recommends reorder quantities to optimize costs?
questions.explanation: Prescriptive analytics recommends decisions or actions subject to objectives and constraints.

questions.q: Which analytics type forecasts SKU-store demand using history and seasonality?
questions.explanation: Predictive analytics forecasts likely future outcomes.
